name: 420Notifications
purpose: Opt-in notification and alert delivery for public 420 Integrated chain, protocol, application and wallet-relevant events without becoming authority for the underlying event or gaining wallet execution rights.

sources.messenger: delivery transport may integrate with 420Messenger, but private message payloads are not notification index input
sources.otherApps: registered public application events and explicit publisher notification feeds

supportedClasses: security, deprecation and contract verification changes

invariants: NOTIFY-INV-001: 420Notifications owns no canonical protocol state and requires no Notifications-specific Genesis contract.
NOTIFY-INV-002: A notification never becomes authority for the event it describes; underlying chain or protocol state remains canonical.
NOTIFY-INV-003: Every actionable notification preserves source provenance and links back to the canonical or registered origin.
NOTIFY-INV-004: 420Notifications cannot sign transactions, approve spending, grant Smart Account capabilities, transfer assets or bypass Wallet confirmation.
NOTIFY-INV-005: User subscriptions are opt-in, reversible and independently controllable by source/topic/severity; promotional notifications require separate consent.
NOTIFY-INV-006: Delivery retry, fan-out and provider failover cannot create duplicate canonical events or mutate the underlying protocol state.
NOTIFY-INV-007: Private Messenger/Commons payloads, encrypted Resource payloads, private Identity fields and raw Attention telemetry are not indexed as notification source data.
NOTIFY-INV-008: Wallet watchlists, notification history and delivery endpoints are private by default and are not published as protocol state.
NOTIFY-INV-009: On-chain notifications identify chain/network and preserve relevant block/transaction/log references plus confirmation/finality context when available.
NOTIFY-INV-010: Reorged, reverted, expired or superseded events can invalidate presentation state through append-only canonicality updates without rewriting finalized canonical history.
NOTIFY-INV-011: Rate limiting, deduplication and abuse controls cannot silently redefine protocol truth; users retain direct Wallet/Explorer/RPC access to canonical state.
NOTIFY-INV-012: Notification service unavailability cannot block payments, swaps, bridges, governance, staking, contract interaction or any other protocol operation.
NOTIFY-INV-013: Alternative notification clients and providers may independently derive and deliver alerts from the same canonical sources.
NOTIFY-INV-014: Replay checkpoints are consumer-owned, chain-bound, opaque and non-authoritative, and advance only after successful batch processing.
